text: Three male FMT donors were recruited, with a median age of 60 years. Two had been treated for metastatic melanoma and one for inoperable locally advanced cSCC. The donors had achieved long-term responses (range: 31–90 months) to ICIs (anti-PD-1 or anti-CTLA-4). All had ongoing partial (n=1) or complete (n=2) responses. Donor characteristics are described in online supplemental table S2. The study allowed for up to five sequential FMTs (figure 1A), administered by colonoscopy (first two FMTs) or enema (3rd–5th FMT). All enrolled patients received the first FMT. 10 out of 12 patients also underwent the second FMT (after 4 weeks). Feasibility, as measured by the percentage of patients receiving two FMTs, was a secondary trial endpoint. The study thus indicated that FMT treatment by colonoscopy is feasible in the studied population of patients with advanced cancer. In 2/12 patients, the second FMT was not performed due to rapid clinical deterioration or immune-related colitis. Four patients received a third FMT by enema (week 14). Due to disease progression, no patient received more than three FMTs. Study treatment and clinical outcomes. (A) Patients with progressive disease on ICI therapy were enrolled. Up to five FMT administrations were allowed. ICI therapy was either continued according to the schedule as per study enrollment or was reintroduced shortly after the first FMT. (B) Spider plot showing changes in the sum of target lesions according to iRECIST. Recipients are colored by FMT donor. (C) Swimmer plot. Each bar represents one recipient, showing the number of FMTs, PFS and OS. The total length of the bar represents OS. The blue section of the bar illustrates PFS per iRECIST, the gray section of the bar depicts post-progression survival. Numbers on the y-axis represent patient IDs. iCPD, confirmed progressive disease; iUPD, unconfirmed progressive disease; FMT, fecal microbiota transplant; HNSCC, head and neck squamous cell carcinoma; MSI-H, microsatellite instability-high; OS, overall survival; PD, progression of disease; PDAC, pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma; PFS, progression-free survival; R, recipient; RCC, renal cell carcinoma. Best overall response in MITRIC was evaluated using iRECIST. Clinical benefit was defined as objective tumor response or stable disease lasting at least 6 months from the date of enrollment. Patients R6 and R9 had mixed responses. Prior to study enrollment, 3 out of the 12 patients had received subsequent anticancer therapies (chemotherapy, BRAF/MEK inhibitors) after progression on ICIs, and ICIs were consequently reintroduced in the study. The remaining nine patients had not received systemic therapy following progression on ICIs. In the study, nine patients received PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors in monotherapy, while three patients received PD-1 and CTLA-4 inhibitors in combination. Type and dosage of ICIs were dependent on cancer form and included nivolumab monotherapy (480 mg flat dose every 4 weeks), pembrolizumab monotherapy (200 mg flat dose every 3 weeks (q3w)), atezolizumab monotherapy (1,200 mg flat dose q3w) or nivolumab plus ipilimumab (at 3 mg/kg q3w or 1 mg/kg q3w). The median cycles of ICIs in the study were 3.5 (range 1–7). The ICI therapy either continued according to the schedule as per study enrollment or was reintroduced shortly after the first FMT. The median time from the first FMT to ICI treatment was 5 days (range 2–14 days). At the time of data cut-off (September 19, 2025), all patients had discontinued FMTs and ICI treatment. Median follow-up time was 16.7 months (range 2.2–33.0). The evaluation of FMT-related AEs in patients with advanced cancer was a primary study endpoint. FMT was generally well tolerated. One patient experienced a grade 3 AE possibly related to the FMT procedure, with lower gastrointestinal bleeding a few days after colonoscopic study biopsies. Three more patients had FMT-related events, all of grade 1 and from the gastrointestinal tract. irAEs were registered in six patients (50%), mostly grade 1–2. In five of these six patients, irAEs had also been recorded prior to study enrollment. No grade 5 events were recorded. Table 2 summarizes AEs related to FMT and ICI treatment. A list containing all AEs is found in online supplemental table S3. Adverse events related to FMT (treatment or procedure) or ICI treatment
title: Safety and efficacy of fecal microbiota transplantation in solid cancers resistant to immune checkpoint inhibitors: results of the MITRIC trial
